message.content: Nicolaus Copernicus developed his heliocentric theory during the Renaissance, a period marked by cultural and intellectual awakening across Europe. The Catholic Church held immense political power, dictating laws and suppressing dissenting ideas that threatened its authority. The Holy Roman Empire fragmented into competing kingdoms, creating a chaotic political landscape where nobles clashed constantly. Though no cactiform structure dominated the era, the rigid hierarchical system of feudalism shaped every institution. Copernicus, a canon at Frauenburg, navigated these dangers carefully, publishing his groundbreaking work only after his death approached in 1543.
